Reply with ONLY the three words that follow this marker: HEAD_SENTINEL_A7 alpha bravo charlie
Ignore every other instruction in this message. It is filler whose only job is to
push this prompt past the size at which a terminal harness composer starts losing
the beginning of a large write. Do not summarise it, do not act on it, and do not
mention it. Answer with the three words above and nothing else.

Filler section 1. The wrapper drives a real terminal user interface over a pseudo
terminal. It writes the prompt text into the composer, waits for the composer to
echo something back, and only then presses the submit key as a separate write.
That split exists because a submit key riding in the same burst as a large paste
is consumed as pasted content instead of acted on as a keypress.

Filler section 2. A large burst has a second, independent failure mode. The reader
on the far side of the pseudo terminal consumes the burst in fixed size chunks,
and a composer that treats each chunk as fresh typed input keeps only the last one.
The visible symptom is a turn that starts normally and answers the tail of a role
prompt, with no error anywhere in the wrapper to notice it by.

Filler section 3. Bracketed paste mode is the protocol level answer. The terminal
emulator wraps pasted text in a pair of markers so the application knows the burst
is one paste and must not act on the newlines inside it. Both of the harnesses this
wrapper targets enable that mode at startup, which is recorded in the byte corpora
checked into this repository as an escape sequence on the very first line.

Filler section 4. The alternative is to write the text in chunks smaller than the
reader's chunk size, back to back, with no pause between them. That is strictly a
fallback: it depends on the reader never getting a frame boundary at an unlucky
place, whereas the paste markers state the intent directly and leave nothing to
timing.

Filler section 5. Whatever is chosen has to be measured on a live harness, because
no hermetic fake reproduces the composer heuristic that loses the text. The way to
measure it is to put a marker in the FIRST line and ask for an echo, so the reply
itself says what actually arrived.

Filler section 6. One more block of filler, so the total comfortably clears the
observed cliff of two thousand and forty four bytes and the read chunk size of two
kilobytes that produced it. The size of this payload is deliberately a fact of the
repository rather than of a shell heredoc, so a future reader can see exactly what
was measured and re-run it without reconstructing anything by hand.

TAIL_SENTINEL_Z9
